sources.note: Silent: 0 occurrences of stress/stressed/unstressed/accent in the whole file. Phupa appears only in sec. 4.5 'The Downriver meso-clade of Riverine Phula' (pp. 15-16: TC-1 shift to /21/ with splits to /33/; /55/ reflexes of the Riverine *checked-tone merger; 'With the exception of Phupa, each of the other three languages in this clade also include *voiceless fricative onset reflexes among the conditioning environments'; Phupa-Phuza micro-clade by *nasal-onset-conditioned TC-2 split to /13/ and /21/). The Downriver phonology sketch is of the sister lect Phuza (sec. 3.2 pp. 6-7: four tonemes /55…

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Change Request 2007-105: create [ypp] Phupa (adopted 2008-01-14), 8 pp., and Request for New Language Code Element [ypp] Phupa, 5 pp. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Identity/classification only: 'Phupa was first described linguistically by Bai (1994).. Phupa stop-final tone reflexes pattern much like Phuza (instead of Muji), but Phuza speakers insist that Phupa is not a dialect of their language.. Not to be confused with Phupha.. or Phuma which belongs to the Muji cluster genetically but also uses the autonym Phupa (for male speakers)' (CR p.3). Sources cited: Bai Bibo 1994, GJMZ 1990, Pelkey 2006, Pelkey forthcoming 2008.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Muji's mirrored merger: correlative redistribution of checked tone classes in a newly defined Burmic cluster. Mon-Khmer Studies 37: 179-195.
sources.note: Silent (0 hits for stress/accent/prominence). Phupa-GMD is the out-group datapoint: 'GMD (Phupa) was first introduced to the Chinese linguistic literature by Bai (1994) along with a suggestion that the variety is affiliated with Muji.. it is missing the key Muji innovations, including the checked-tone redistribution pattern'; 'The GMD data shows virtually no evidence of incorporating the Muji cluster innovation.' References give Bai Bibo 1994 in full (Yunnan Minzu Xueyuan Zengkan 1994: 80-93).
